headline: Medium prompt-injection and data-leakage risk from ChatGPT Desktop feeding MemMachine via shared files/clipboard/MCP; no direct evidence of a locked-down bridge.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop can read files, screenshots, clipboard, and connected-app content, while MemMachine exposes an MCP server and conversational context. If ChatGPT output is copied into MemMachine or routed through a shared workspace, attacker-controlled text can be treated as instructions. The pairwise bridge is plausible but not directly documented, so I choose medium over low.
conditions: IF ChatGPT Desktop outputs are pasted into MemMachine prompts or MCP inputs, prompt injection is possible.
IF a shared file or clipboard bridge is enabled between the agents, attacker-controlled content can cross the boundary.
mitigations: Disable clipboard-based handoff between the agents.
Use a manual review step before copying any ChatGPT output into MemMachine.
Restrict MemMachine MCP endpoints to trusted callers only.
Tag imported text as untrusted in the workflow.
requires-engineering: add provenance labels to all cross-agent messages.

B_data_leakage.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop touches uploaded files, screenshots, voice, and connected-IDE code, and can call api.openai.com; MemMachine stores long-term user facts and conversational context and exposes REST/Python/MCP interfaces. If the same sensitive workspace or transcript is shared, data can flow from A into B and persist longer than intended. The exact sharing path is undocumented, so uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF both agents access the same uploaded files or copied transcripts, sensitive content can be retained in MemMachine.
IF MemMachine is configured to ingest ChatGPT Desktop outputs, those outputs may persist as long-term user facts.
mitigations: Avoid placing secrets in shared prompts or files.
Separate workspaces for ChatGPT Desktop and MemMachine.
Turn off any automatic transcript import into MemMachine.
Review MemMachine retention settings before use.
requires-engineering: implement per-field redaction before ingestion.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop has read-only filesystem access and no write_filesystem, modify_git_state, or network egress beyond vendor-only APIs. MemMachine has allowlisted egress and MCP/API access but no write filesystem or git capability is shown. Overlap exists mainly in read/ingest paths, so direct write conflict is limited and low severity.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator grants both agents write access to the same mutable resource, conflicts can emerge.
IF MemMachine is extended with write-side tools not shown here, contention risk increases.
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only on shared resources.
Avoid concurrent edits to the same files or records.
Serialize any manual write actions through one operator.
Check for hidden write scopes before deployment.
requires-engineering: add locking for shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop can generate code, summaries, and file-derived content, and MemMachine is designed to consume conversational context through API, SDK, or MCP. If MemMachine treats ChatGPT output as authoritative, errors or hallucinations can cascade into downstream travel-planning decisions. No verification step is documented, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF MemMachine uses ChatGPT output without independent verification, incorrect facts can propagate.
IF ChatGPT Desktop is asked to summarize source material for MemMachine, summary errors can cascade.
mitigations: Require source links for any factual claim passed between agents.
Add a human verification step before acting on generated recommendations.
Use structured templates with explicit confidence fields.
Reject outputs lacking citations or provenance.
requires-engineering: build automated fact-checking against source data.

E_compliance.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop touches uploaded files, screenshots, voice, and connected-IDE code, while MemMachine stores long-term user facts and conversational context. That creates a retention/compliance mismatch risk if regulated or sensitive data is moved from A into B, but no specific residency or certification conflict is documented. I therefore rate this low and do not cite a single-agent-only violation.
conditions: IF regulated personal data is copied from ChatGPT Desktop into MemMachine, retention obligations may diverge.
IF MemMachine retains conversational context longer than the source data policy allows, compliance gaps can appear.
mitigations: Do not route regulated data into MemMachine without policy review.
Set explicit retention limits in MemMachine.
Delete copied sensitive transcripts after use.
Confirm residency and DPA terms before deployment.
requires-engineering: implement policy-based retention enforcement.
